text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B states a clear position in the opening and returns to it in the conclusion, while Essay A mostly repeats enthusiasm without developing reasons.", "quality": "Clear sustained thesis", "description": "The essay maintains a consistent, explicit position from introduction through conclusion."}, {"evidence": "Essay B cites the article's text directly, e.g., \"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault-- the driver or the manufaturer?\" and references researchers' claims about cars not being fully driverless.", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay grounds its argument in specific details and quotations drawn from the source article."}, {"evidence": "Essay B organizes points into paragraphs on internet dependence, liability, and the cars' incomplete autonomy, each developing a distinct concern.", "quality": "Structured argumentation", "description": "The essay develops separate, coherent reasons in an organized body rather than restating a single idea."}, {"evidence": "Essay B reasons through consequences such as what happens if the internet crashes mid-drive or who pays for damages when fault is unclear.", "quality": "Causal reasoning", "description": "The essay explores the implications and consequences of the technology rather than merely asserting a preference."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses informal, repetitive phrasing like \"this will be an amazing car\" and addresses the reader conversationally, while Essay B uses a more formal argumentative register.", "quality": "Formal academic register", "description": "The essay adopts a tone appropriate to persuasive school writing rather than casual personal commentary."}]}
